decision.summary: The default playable launch now shows a restrained savanna tree line and countable low bank cover without the rejected waterline canopy or camera-clipped silhouette. The coarse terrain, synthetic vegetation, flat water, sparse near-field cover, and missing reviewed Batoka ecology remain below the photoreal bar.

evidence.capture_path: default runnable gameplay camera with raft and crew; no diagnostic camera override

upper_quarter_green_pixel_heuristic.definition: Pixels in the upper 25 percent with G greater than 1.12 times R, G greater than 1.08 times B, and G greater than 45; baseline letterbox removed before analysis.
upper_quarter_green_pixel_heuristic.interpretation: The heuristic corroborates visible ridgeline ecology only; it is not a photoreal or species-fidelity metric.

ground_cover.related_ground_cover_shadow_policy: full-corridor ground cover and the documentary camera mosaic are also shadowless; downstream woody ecology retains shadows

woody_ecology.shadow_exception_scope: runnable launch window only; prevents near-camera crown/wall streaks under the low review sun

rejected_iterations.reason: Rejected: cover was pasted onto steep faces and woody silhouettes visibly occupied the right waterline.
Rejected: hard gates reduced invalid cover, but a near launch canopy cluster still read as standing in water and a clipped dark silhouette crossed the left wall.
Rejected: broader lateral clearance increased safe candidates but retained the near-camera composition defect.

remaining_external_acceptance_gates: Guide and geospatial approval of the playable centerline, stationing, access, portage, and rescue context.
Rights approval for all terrain, imagery, supplied-map, vegetation, and reference inputs.
Higher-resolution full-reach terrain or reviewed field-capture derivative replacing the 30 m DSM approximation.
Southern African gorge-woodland species, density, age, wind, season, and wetness approval.
Production terrain, vegetation, rock, water, breaking-water, foam, spray, mist, and lighting art approval.
Validated seasonal hydraulics, bathymetry, guide lines, hazard readability, and rescue behavior.
Measured packaged desktop and target-VR visual/performance acceptance.
